statement: A match played in the solo, couch or any other non-LAN desktop game saves no replay: the only recorder outside LAN is a patch the private browser page applies to a scratch copy of the host.
evidence: commit:8901d351 (git grep 'bb_on|_bb_arm' -- render sim ui net: no match; git grep 'SimReplay.(play|recorder)' outside tools: net/desync.gd and qa/ only)
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (the recorder already exists as a patch; the work is moving it into the host behind a switch and choosing where files go)
risk: A recorder that touches the tick loop could change timing; known early by the golden gate and replay_xproc_check staying green.
orb_question: Should every desktop match keep its replay on the player's PC automatically (the last 20 or so, nothing sent)? Recommended: yes.

statement: The replay itself names no build: it carries a format number, an input-layout number and a hash of the data, so a replay from a build with the same data but different code is not refused up front and only fails later as a state mismatch.
risk: If the build id were folded into the data hash it would change the LAN match key and refuse every older file; known early by parity.gd's replay cases.

statement: No record on file shows a replay saved by the baseline build verifying to its last tick on that build, and the first real LAN save has not been put through the report tool.
evidence: commit:8901d351 (grep 'BLACKBOX OK' under docs/*/runs/6a30b4c9: no match)
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (two headless playbacks with the tools that exist)
risk: A real play file may not reproduce on its own build; known the first time blackbox-verify is run on one.

statement: Settings surviving a restart has never been tested across a real restart, on Windows or on Linux: the only tests rebuild the screen inside one process, and they run in the local gate, not in CI.
depends_on: F-PERF-01, F-PERF-02 (a desktop and a Linux build to test on)
risk: The user folder may behave differently on a Deck (path, permissions, suspend); known early by one two-run test on the Linux build.

statement: On main the lock that keeps Reduce flashing on is switched off, so a saved Off is read back at start-up, and every build shares one settings folder, so an Off saved in an earlier build carries into a later one.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (a data switch and a check on the candidate's packed data)
risk: A tester's build could start with full effects from an old file; known early by reading the candidate's packed features data.

statement: The settings file and the controls file are overwritten in place, so a write cut short (power loss, a crash) leaves an unreadable file and every remembered choice silently returns to its default.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (the cache already writes to a temporary file and renames)
risk: Low; a Deck that runs out of battery mid-write is the likely case.

statement: Neither settings file has a way to change shape between builds: the settings file has no version, and a controls file whose schema number is not 1 is treated as absent and overwritten at the next save.
risk: The first change of shape after Alpha wipes testers' remaps without a word; known when a schema 2 is first proposed.

statement: Three loaders do not check the types of what they read (a replay's seed, ticks, toggles and checkpoints; a controls file's preset entries; a slider option saved as text), and what an exported build does with such a file is not evidenced.
risk: A hand-edited file could stop start-up or a tool with a script error; known early by a small set of broken files fed to each loader.

statement: The settings file is opened and parsed again on per-frame paths (the beam reminder after 45 seconds and the first-use hints), as the safety audit of 2026-11-07 noted, and this is unchanged at the baseline.
risk: A per-frame file read costs more on a Deck's storage than on a desktop; not measured.

statement: LAN match files and the LAN log grow without a cap: a file is written at every match end, pause, quit and report into a folder beside the program, and the log is appended to.
risk: A long session fills the folder; a folder beside the program may not be writable where a tester installs it (the save then returns nothing, net/lan.gd:531-533).

statement: Where the game keeps its files on a tester's PC is written nowhere a tester would read, and the folder is the engine's default one named after the working title, so a change of title would leave settings behind.
risk: A tester asked to clear or send their settings cannot find them; removing the game leaves the files.

statement: The checks that guard saved files (settings and remap persistence, the controls file, the cache's tamper cases) are not in CI; their only saved result at the baseline is the EP's local gate output.
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml (no line names hud_check, remap_test, field_cache_check or planet_cache_check)
risk: A change that breaks persistence lands unseen when the local gate is skipped.

statement: A choice made on the Settings screen is written at once and applied again at the next start, with unknown keys skipped and out-of-range or retired values pulled to a valid one.
Remapped controls are saved per player to their own file and applied at start-up, with unknown or retired layouts and unknown actions dropped and listed.
A missing, unreadable or non-dictionary settings or controls file is treated as nothing remembered, and the start menu's saved choices are clamped to valid ones.

Replay playback refuses, without running, a file of another format, version or input layout, a malformed input entry, a slot the match lacks, and a replay recorded on other data, and CI tests each case.
Replays recorded in one process play back in a fresh process, in CI with a negative control, and the baseline's local gate has the pass on file.
A LAN match file names its build in its body and in its file name, and the browser page's match file is stamped with its build, so the wrapper around a replay already says which build made it.
Two LAN PCs cannot start a match on different data: the match key both must share includes the same data hash the replay carries.

The planet cache on disk is well defended: each file is keyed by the data hash and the engine version, carries a checksum, is spot-checked against fresh values on load, is written through a temporary file, and old files are removed past a kept count.
Saved files are plain JSON read with the JSON parser only, no saved file is loaded as code or as an engine resource, and nothing in the game code sends a saved file anywhere.
When the Reduce flashing lock is on, a saved Off is ignored on load and the Settings and menu routes cannot write Off, and a test covers it.
